citeAs: Rajpurkar, P., Zhang, J., Lopyrev, K., and Liang, P. (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. EMNLP 2016.
creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang (Stanford University)
description: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset) is a reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs posed by crowdworkers on 536 Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text (span) from the corresponding reading passage. The dataset covers a wide range of topics and answer types, and is designed to challenge machine reading comprehension systems.
name: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset)
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question in the development and test sets has at least 3 answers total (1 original + at least 2 additional). Training set questions have 1 answer each.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers located in the United States or Canada, with a 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs completed on Amazon Mechanical Turk.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was assessed using inter-annotator agreement: the second answer to each question was treated as the human prediction, with the other answers as ground truth. Human performance on the test set was 77.0% exact match and 86.8% F1. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada. Workers were asked to spend 4 minutes on every paragraph and paid $9 per hour. On each paragraph, workers asked and answered up to 5 questions on the content. Questions had to be entered in a text field and answers highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were provided sample paragraphs and examples of good and bad questions. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words (copy-paste from paragraph was disabled). For additional answers, workers selected the shortest span answering each question, or marked it unanswerable.
rai:dataBiases: Crowdworkers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words (copy-paste was disabled) to reduce lexical overlap bias between questions and passages. Annotators were restricted to US/Canada residents with high HIT acceptance rates, which may introduce demographic bias. The dataset is sourced exclusively from English Wikipedia, limiting topic and style diversity.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected in three stages: (1) Passage curation: top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles by PageRank were obtained, 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random, paragraphs were extracted (stripping images, figures, tables, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters), yielding 23,215 paragraphs. Articles were partitioned into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. (2) Question-answer collection: crowdworkers on the Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk as backend) were asked to write and answer up to 5 questions per paragraph. (3) Additional answers collection: at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10,000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks. From these, 536 articles were sampled, and individual paragraphs were extracted (excluding images, figures, tables, and paragraphs shorter than 500 characters), resulting in 23,215 paragraphs.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataLimitations: Answers are constrained to be spans from the passage, which is more restrictive than free-form answers. 77.3% of correct answers are constituents in the constituency parse; the remaining answers are not directly representable as constituents. 2.6% of questions in the development and test sets were marked unanswerable by at least one crowdworker. The dataset does not provide answer choices, requiring systems to select from all possible spans.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Wikipedia articles were preprocessed by extracting individual paragraphs and stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to drive progress toward natural language understanding and machine reading comprehension. By providing a large, high-quality benchmark, it encourages development of more expressive models that can understand text and answer questions, with potential downstream benefits for information retrieval and question answering systems.
rai:dataUseCases: Reading comprehension and question answering research; training and evaluating machine learning models for natural language understanding; benchmarking progress on span-based question answering from passages.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses and POS tags for answer categorization, and NER tags for classifying proper noun phrases into person, location, and other entities. Dependency parse trees were also generated by Stanford CoreNLP for syntactic divergence analysis.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling beyond noting that paragraphs shorter than 500 characters were discarded (covered in preprocessing).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper does not specify exact dates for data collection; only mentions results over "the last four months (since June 2016)" for model improvements, not collection timeframe.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation or augmentation described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan described beyond the initial release.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of Wikipedia article passages and crowdsourced questions/answers; no personal or sensitive information is collected or discussed.
